subject: Post-call recap + model-mix / token volumes / pricing next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks for the demo — quick recap + ask on volumes/model mix

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and a few asks so we can put together a tailored pricing estimate and pilot plan: 

Recap:
- You showed search + summarization flows where users type queries; embeddings + similarity search power the retrieval, chat model surfaces the final answer, and you use a reranker for top-k precision.
- Primary users: customer support agents and power-search for CS; estimated 150k monthly active users eventually.
- Peak window is Pacific business hours, ~3–4x baseline.

Asks (to size pricing & model mix):
1) Rough monthly token volumes by model type (chat generation vs. embedding units vs. rerank tokens). If you can give current prod numbers + 12-mo target that'd be ideal.
2) Budget range for LLM infrastructure (monthly) or target $/1M tokens you want us to aim for in an evaluation.
3) Any constraints: on-prem requirement, SOC2 controls, or PII retention concerns.

Goal: we’ll return a simple model-mix pricing estimate (per-model unit economics, projected monthly spend) and a 2-week pilot scope you can share internally. I’ve looped Dev (SE) to help with throughput/latency sizing.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — quick recap + ask on volumes/model mix

Marissa —

Great recap, thanks. Below are the rough numbers we discussed on the call (current -> 12mo target):

- Chat (user-facing generations): 30M tokens/month current -> 120M tokens/month target
- Embeddings (indexing + retrieval): 1.2M embedding vectors/month current -> 6M/month target
- Rerank (scoring top-k results): ~200k rerank requests/month -> 1M/month target
- Peak concurrency: expect ~250 concurrent requests during peak (we're on K8s + autoscale today)
- Budget: right now leadership is thinking in the $10k–$15k/month range for hosted LLM infrastructure; open to seeing unit economics to adjust.

A few clarifications: embeddings are billed per vector in our forecast, while chat is token-based. For rerank we typically count the tokens processed by the reranker model (short sequences). Happy for you to propose target $/1M tokens (or $/1M units for embeddings) that would make sense for a pilot.

Also attaching our SOC2 questionnaire — security will want to review that before any pilot.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Director of Product, Acme Corp
alexj@acme.com

Attachments: SOC2-questionnaire.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alexj@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — quick recap + ask on volumes/model mix

Alex — thanks for the detail, this is great and makes sizing straightforward. High-level pricing and model-mix estimate below (we'll put the numbers into the attached XLS):

Assumptions used:
- Chat = standard chat completion model mix (we can propose a cost-optimized variant for scale)
- Embeddings = high-quality embedding model for retrieval (charged per vector)
- Rerank = small specialized model; charged per token processed (short sequences)
- We apply batching and prefix-KV caching where possible; numbers below reflect expected batching gains at your concurrency profile.

Rough target unit economics (ballpark for proposal):
- Chat: $1,200 per 1M tokens (optimized mix / reserved pricing estimate) — flexible depending on model variant (higher for newest LLMs, lower for quantized variants)
- Embeddings: $250 per 1M vectors (note: per-vector price; we express as $/1M units)
- Rerank: $400 per 1M tokens processed (short sequences, lower effective token count per request)

Using your 12-mo targets (Chat 120M tokens / Embeddings 6M vectors / Rerank 1M requests):
- Chat spend (est): $144k/month
- Embeddings spend (est): $1.5k/month
- Rerank spend (est): $0.4k/month
- Total (hosted estimate): ~$146k/month — this is list-ish; with reserved capacity and commitment discounts we can get closer to your $10k–$15k target depending on tradeoffs (e.g., model mix, quantization, or Dedicated capacity).

Alternative scenarios to approach your $10k–$15k target:
- Start with a tiered approach: embeddings + small rerank on Hosted, pilot chat on a smaller model for 2 weeks to validate quality.
- Use quantized model variant for chat (reduces per-token cost ~3–4x) at modest quality tradeoff.
- Relevant: dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit) can reduce per-token cost materially for high baseline volumes.

Next steps we suggest:
1) Dev & Rishi to propose a 2-week pilot plan (technical POC + cost monitoring) and a sample SOW.
2) We’ll share a pricing XLS that shows sensitivity (model mix, quantization, reserved discount) and a target $/1M tokens for each scenario.
3) Security review: we'll complete SOC2 questionnaire and propose an NDA + pilot agreement.

Attached: Redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx (ballpark model-mix calc), pilot-scope-2wk.docx

If this looks ok, we'll schedule a short wrap call to align stakeholders and finalize pilot dates.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: Redwood-pricing-estimate.xlsx, pilot-scope-2wk.docx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — quick recap + ask on volumes/model mix

Alex — quick technical note on model-mix and cost levers: 

- For chat: recommend mixing a 13B quantized variant for the majority of traffic and a smaller percentage hitting a higher-quality 34B family for hard queries. With your peak concurrency (~250) we can get batching of ~6–8 average which helps unit cost.
- For embeddings: choose the higher-quality vector for retrieval; we can downsample older content or use a lightweight vector for low-priority indices to reduce costs.
- For rerank: small transformer, keep context short — cost per request is tiny once you optimize top-k.

I’ll sync with Dev to include estimated effective batching multipliers in the XLS so the $/1M tokens reflects real throughput gains. Happy to jump on a short call with your infra team to validate latency/SLA expectations.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
